practiceNotes: Spaced repetition should maintain definitions, representations, assumptions and method selection; passing recall checks does not establish proof, programming, laboratory or field competence.
Assess extended work separately through proofs, executable tests, laboratory records, reproducible analyses and oral defense of modeling decisions.

Chemical, electrical, optical and biological experiments require appropriate facilities, risk review, supervision, waste handling and locally authorized procedures; these conditions are not assumed satisfied.

Human-participant, animal, environmental-sampling and sensitive-genomic projects require applicable consent, permits, ethics approval and data governance. Use approved public, synthetic or de-identified evidence when authorization is unavailable.

Security practice must use owned or explicitly authorized isolated systems. Robotics, high voltage, lasers, radiation and pathogenic organisms require additional operational authorization; simulations do not certify practical handling competence.

Provided instruments and numerical packages may support bounded applications where stated. Implementation and proof outcomes require separate student-produced algorithms and arguments, not software output alone.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Living Systems
decks.description: Recognize biological organization and evaluate elementary biological evidence.

includes: Cell-to-ecosystem organization, biological diversity, inheritance and evidence-based explanations at introductory depth.

practice: Maintain an observation notebook and defend competing explanations for an organismal or ecological pattern.

outcomes.description: Distinguish bacteria, archaea, protists, fungi, plants and animals using observable traits and interpret a branching ancestry diagram.
Separate observation from explanation; propose controls and compare evolutionary or physiological claims against observations.
Explain cells, organisms and ecosystems through matter exchange, energy use, information inheritance and feedback.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Foundations
decks.description: Write, explain and test small programs.

includes: Executable programming with locally taught arithmetic, state, control flow, recursion, collections and testing.

practice: Implement a file-based data-processing application with tests, error handling and a written execution trace.

outcomes.description: Represent records, sequences and key-value collections; parse files and transform data while handling malformed input.
Specify input-output behavior, construct boundary tests and use traces and a debugger to isolate defects.
Trace and write typed expressions, variables, branches, loops, functions and terminating recursive procedures.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Discrete Foundations and Proof
decks.description: Construct rigorous arguments about discrete objects.

includes: Logic, sets, functions, proof techniques, finite counting and elementary graphs.

practice: Write independently checked proofs and construct counterexamples for false counting, relation and graph conjectures.

outcomes.description: Count finite arrangements using bijections, products, combinations and inclusion-exclusion; derive and solve elementary recurrences.
Translate quantified statements and prove set or function claims using direct proof, contradiction, contrapositive and induction.
Represent relations, trees and graphs; prove basic connectivity, equivalence-relation and tree properties.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Quantitative Foundations
decks.description: Represent and solve elementary quantitative problems.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, elementary functions, coordinate geometry and dimensional reasoning.

practice: Build and check a unit-consistent model from a diagram and data table, comparing graphical and algebraic solutions.

outcomes.description: Calculate with fractions, powers and logarithms; rearrange formulas and solve linear, quadratic and simultaneous linear equations.
Translate tables, graphs and formulas for polynomial, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions; interpret inverse functions and rates.
Calculate lengths, areas, volumes, vectors and angles in Cartesian coordinates; convert units and check dimensional consistency.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Matter and Chemical Representation
decks.description: Connect chemical composition to particle and bonding models.

includes: Atomic composition, periodicity, bonding models, molecular representations and chemical amount calculations.

practice: Infer an unknown composition from mass and reaction data, explaining where particle and bonding models cease to be reliable.

outcomes.description: Construct Lewis structures, resonance forms and three-dimensional molecular shapes; predict polarity and intermolecular interactions.
Relate isotopes, ions and electron configurations to periodic trends using an explicitly limited shell model.
Balance equations and calculate moles, concentrations, limiting reagents, yields and ideal-gas quantities with units.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
decks.description: Implement and justify efficient algorithms.

includes: Data structures, graph algorithms, algorithmic paradigms and correctness/resource analysis.

practice: Implement competing graph algorithms, prove their contracts and benchmark sparse and dense instances.

outcomes.description: Prove correctness using invariants and induction; derive asymptotic and amortized bounds and compare measured scaling.
Implement sorting, graph traversal, shortest paths and dynamic programming using explicit array, graph and table states.
Implement lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, heaps and search trees; justify representation invariants and operation costs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Systems and Architecture
decks.description: Explain computation from gates to machine programs.

includes: Digital logic, binary arithmetic, instruction execution, assembly and memory hierarchy.

practice: Build a small processor in a logic simulator and optimize an assembly kernel without changing its tested behavior.

outcomes.description: Construct combinational and sequential Boolean circuits; encode integers and floating-point numbers and diagnose overflow and rounding.
Trace a stored-program processor and write assembly using registers, stacks, calling conventions and addressing modes.
Analyze caches, pipelines and memory layout; measure how locality and dependencies affect execution time.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Single-Variable Calculus
decks.description: Calculate and interpret continuous change and accumulation.

includes: Limits, single-variable differentiation, integration, approximation and series.

practice: Derive and compare exact, graphical and approximate solutions for an accumulation and optimization model.

outcomes.description: Calculate limits and derivatives, including implicit derivatives; solve optimization and related-rate problems with interpretation.
Evaluate definite, indefinite and improper integrals using substitution and integration by parts; apply the fundamental theorem.
Test elementary series convergence and construct Taylor approximations with suitable remainder estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Linear Algebra
decks.description: Represent and solve linear problems geometrically and algebraically.

includes: Finite-dimensional real and complex vector spaces, matrices, inner products and spectral decompositions.

practice: Solve a least-squares reconstruction problem and prove when its coefficient vector is unique.

outcomes.description: Perform elimination and matrix operations; characterize rank, null spaces, determinants and solvability.
Construct bases and linear maps, prove elementary vector-space claims and change coordinates; calculate orthogonal projections.
Use locally defined complex arithmetic to calculate eigenvalues, diagonalizations and singular-value decompositions; solve least-squares problems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability and Data
decks.description: Reason about uncertainty and elementary empirical evidence.

includes: Finite probability, descriptive statistics, sampling, bounded introductory inference and study design without calculus.

practice: Design a randomized comparison and use a provided resampling tool to assess uncertainty, bias and practical effect size.

outcomes.description: Use stated binomial, normal-approximation and bootstrap procedures for intervals and tests; check conditions, multiplicity and sampling design.
Construct finite sample spaces using locally taught counting rules; calculate conditional probabilities, Bayes updates, expectations and variances.
Summarize and visualize data; distinguish association, sampling variation, confounding and measurement error.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Physical Models and Measurement
decks.description: Build and test elementary physical models.

includes: Calculus-free mechanics, energy, DC circuits, measurement and uncertainty.

practice: Measure a pendulum or cart and a resistor network; compare predictions with uncertainty and justify a safe measurement configuration.

outcomes.description: Apply charge conservation, voltage and resistance models to series-parallel DC circuits; measure voltage and current safely.
Calibrate a simple instrument, report units and uncertainty, fit a straight line with a provided tool and inspect residuals.
Use position-time graphs, free-body diagrams, constant-acceleration equations and energy balances for one- and two-dimensional motion.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology
decks.description: Explain cellular organization and observe cells quantitatively.

includes: Cell structures, macromolecular functions, membranes, organelles, cell division and basic microscopy.

practice: Quantify cells or organelles from calibrated micrographs and propose controlled tests of a transport or division hypothesis.

outcomes.description: Trace membrane transport, energy conversion, intracellular trafficking and cell-cycle events using compartment and process diagrams.
Relate membranes, organelles, cytoskeleton and macromolecular structures to prokaryotic and eukaryotic cellular functions.
Prepare approved specimens, calibrate light microscopy and estimate cell dimensions and counts while distinguishing artifacts from structures.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolution and Ecology
decks.description: Explain biological change and ecological patterns using models and field evidence.

includes: Evolutionary mechanisms, phylogenetic reasoning, ecological organization, discrete population models and field sampling.

practice: Collect approved field observations or analyze supplied survey records; compare ecological models and defend the sampling design.

outcomes.description: Calculate discrete population growth and life-table projections; explain species interactions, food webs, productivity and nutrient cycles.
Compare selection, drift, migration and speciation explanations; construct small parsimony trees from character matrices and interpret fossil evidence.
Design quadrat, transect and mark-recapture studies; estimate abundance and diversity while evaluating detection and sampling bias.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Reactions and Laboratory Foundations
decks.description: Calculate reaction behavior and obtain defensible laboratory evidence.

includes: Aqueous equilibrium, acid-base and redox reactions, introductory rates and safe quantitative laboratory methods.

practice: Perform an approved titration and rate experiment with controls, uncertainty estimates, full records and a defensible waste plan.

outcomes.description: Calculate acid-base, buffer, solubility and coupled equilibrium compositions using mass balance, charge balance and equilibrium constants.
Prepare solutions, titrate and isolate products; document uncertainty and justify handling, waste and emergency decisions from hazard evidence.
Balance redox reactions and infer empirical rate laws and reaction orders from concentration-time or initial-rate data.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Artificial Intelligence
decks.description: Construct agents using symbolic and probabilistic models.

includes: Heuristic search, constraints, logical knowledge representation, probabilistic inference and sequential decisions.

practice: Build a bounded planning agent and compare symbolic and probabilistic decisions under uncertainty and misspecified objectives.

outcomes.description: Formulate finite Markov decision processes; implement value iteration and tabular reinforcement learning and evaluate reward-design failures.
Represent knowledge with propositional and first-order rules; implement unification, resolution and finite Bayesian-network inference.
Implement heuristic graph search, adversarial search and constraint propagation; justify completeness and optimality under stated conditions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Theory of Computation
decks.description: Prove computational capabilities and limitations.

includes: Automata, formal grammars, computability, reductions and introductory complexity theory.

practice: Write complete reductions with instance encodings, size bounds and both directions of correctness.

outcomes.description: Define time, space, P and NP; construct polynomial reductions and prove NP-completeness for explicit decision problems.
Encode computation with Turing machines; prove undecidability using diagonalization and many-one reductions.
Construct finite and pushdown automata and grammars; prove language closure, equivalence and nonregularity results.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Database Systems
decks.description: Design and implement reliable data management.

includes: Relational modeling, SQL, query processing, indexing and transactions.

practice: Build a small relational application and storage prototype; test queries, concurrent anomalies and crash recovery.

outcomes.description: Implement elementary scans and joins; explain B-tree indexing and compare query plans using cardinality and I/O costs.
Translate requirements into relational schemas; use functional dependencies, normalization, relational algebra and SQL queries.
Analyze schedules for isolation anomalies; implement a bounded transaction log and recovery procedure with stated failure assumptions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Graphics
decks.description: Construct images from geometric scene representations.

includes: Three-dimensional geometry, projective cameras, rasterization, visibility, shading and sampled light transport.

practice: Build a software renderer and compare rasterized and ray-based images using geometric, energy and sampling checks.

outcomes.description: Represent meshes, curves and rigid transforms; derive homogeneous camera projections and interpolate geometric attributes.
Implement clipping, triangle rasterization, depth buffering and texture sampling with explicit aliasing and coordinate conventions.
Implement ray intersections and local illumination; estimate diffuse light transport using a locally taught bounded random-sampling procedure and test convergence empirically.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction
decks.description: Design and evaluate interfaces around human capabilities and obligations.

includes: Interaction design, accessibility, qualitative research, usability experiments and participatory judgment.

practice: Iterate an accessible interface after an approved usability study; submit coded observations, effect estimates and a design rationale.

outcomes.description: Conduct interviews, code qualitative observations and run a counterbalanced usability study with uncertainty-aware quantitative analysis.
Translate user tasks into prototypes using cognitive, perceptual and accessibility principles; implement an interactive prototype.
Compare designs for exclusion, manipulation, consent and privacy; justify tradeoffs using participant evidence and competing stakeholder interests.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Languages and Compilers
decks.description: Implement a language and explain its execution semantics.

includes: Language semantics, functional programming, parsing, type checking, intermediate representations and code generation.

practice: Build a small compiler and interpreter; compare execution on generated tests and document semantic preservation for one optimization.

outcomes.description: Lower syntax into control-flow intermediate code; implement elementary dataflow optimization, register allocation and runtime support.
Define a context-free grammar and implement tokenization, parsing, symbol resolution and static type checking.
Define evaluation rules, lexical scope, closures and types; compare functional, imperative and object-based program behavior.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks
decks.description: Construct and diagnose packet-based communication.

includes: Layered networks, routing, transport, sockets and empirical network diagnosis.

practice: Construct a local network experiment, inject packet loss and explain observed application behavior from packet traces.

outcomes.description: Interpret packet captures and calculate latency, throughput and congestion effects; isolate faults using controlled experiments.
Trace framing, addressing, forwarding, routing and name resolution across link, network and application layers.
Implement a socket application and bounded reliable transport with sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and flow control.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems
decks.description: Implement and reason about operating-system mechanisms.

includes: Processes, system calls, synchronization, scheduling, virtual memory and file systems.

practice: Extend a teaching kernel and reproduce concurrency and memory failures with deterministic tests.

outcomes.description: Implement thread synchronization with locks, condition variables and semaphores; prove bounded protocols free of specified races or deadlocks.
Trace privilege transitions, interrupts and process state; implement and compare CPU scheduling policies.
Analyze paging, allocation and file-system structures; implement a bounded virtual-memory or file-system component.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Software Engineering
decks.description: Deliver maintainable software with justified quality and risk decisions.

includes: Requirements, modular design, collaborative development, software validation and professional responsibility.

practice: Develop a team application with requirements traceability, reviewed changes, automated tests and a documented release-risk decision.

outcomes.description: Elicit requirements, design interfaces and modular architecture, and manage changes through version control and code review.
Analyze privacy, accessibility, licensing and safety consequences; justify release decisions against stakeholder obligations and evidence.
Construct unit, integration, property-based and regression tests; diagnose failures and establish reproducible builds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebra and Number Theory
decks.description: Analyze algebraic structure and arithmetic using proofs and constructions.

includes: Groups, rings, fields, polynomial algebra and elementary number theory.

practice: Classify small algebraic structures and solve arithmetic problems with both constructive calculations and proofs.

outcomes.description: Prove divisibility and congruence results; apply Euclidean algorithms, Chinese remaindering and quadratic residues to integer problems.
Compute subgroups, quotients and group actions; prove homomorphism, orbit-stabilizer and finite-group results.
Analyze ideals, quotient rings, polynomial factorization and field extensions with explicit examples and structural proofs.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Equations
decks.description: Formulate and solve finite-dimensional dynamical models.

includes: Scalar ODEs, linear systems, phase-plane methods, forced oscillations and transforms.

practice: Derive a coupled dynamical model, solve its linear approximation and compare stability predictions with plotted trajectories.

outcomes.description: Solve separable, first-order linear and constant-coefficient second-order initial-value problems; check existence assumptions and units.
Solve linear systems using eigenstructure; analyze nonlinear equilibria through locally defined Jacobian linearization and phase planes.
Use Laplace transforms and Fourier-series forcing to calculate transient, resonant and steady responses of linear systems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus
decks.description: Calculate with scalar and vector fields in several dimensions.

includes: Partial derivatives, multiple integrals, coordinate transformations and vector calculus.

practice: Calculate flux and circulation by direct parameterization and integral theorems, explaining coordinate and orientation choices.

outcomes.description: Calculate gradients, Jacobians and Hessians; apply multivariable chain rules and constrained extrema using Lagrange multipliers.
Evaluate double and triple integrals in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates with correct Jacobians.
Calculate line and surface integrals, divergence and curl; apply Green, Stokes and divergence theorems with oriented boundaries.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Methods and Optimization
decks.description: Implement stable numerical calculations and optimization methods.

includes: Floating-point error, root finding, interpolation, quadrature, numerical linear algebra and finite-dimensional optimization.

practice: Implement an error-controlled numerical library and compare algorithms on ill-conditioned linear, nonlinear and optimization problems.

outcomes.description: Implement bisection, Newton iteration, interpolation and quadrature; derive basic error estimates and distinguish conditioning from stability.
Implement pivoted elimination and QR least squares; measure residuals, conditioning and floating-point error.
Define multivariable gradients locally; implement gradient and Newton optimization, constrained projection and linear-programming simplex pivots; check optimality conditions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis
decks.description: Prove the analytical foundations of calculus.

includes: Completeness, metric convergence, rigorous calculus and sequences of functions.

practice: Produce rigorous proofs and counterexample portfolios for convergence and interchange claims.

outcomes.description: Prove mean-value, differentiability and Riemann-integration results, stating hypotheses and constructing counterexamples when they fail.
Distinguish pointwise and uniform convergence; justify interchanging limits, integrals and derivatives under explicit sufficient conditions.
Use completeness and epsilon arguments to prove convergence, compactness and continuity results in real and metric spaces.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Classical Mechanics
decks.description: Predict motion from forces and conservation laws.

includes: Calculus-based particle motion, conservation laws, rigid-body rotation and gravitation.

practice: Analyze a two-dimensional collision and rotating apparatus, comparing force integration with conservation-law solutions.

outcomes.description: Derive gravitational potentials and effective radial energy for central forces; calculate circular orbits and orbital turning points.
Formulate vector Newton equations in Cartesian and polar coordinates; calculate trajectories, work, impulse and collisions.
Calculate centers of mass, inertia tensors in simple geometries, torque, angular momentum and rigid-body energy.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Thermal Physics
decks.description: Apply macroscopic and elementary microscopic thermal models.

includes: Heat, work, entropy, thermodynamic cycles, kinetic gases and thermal radiation.

practice: Analyze calorimetry and a thermal spectrum, checking energy conservation, entropy production and parameter uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Derive ideal-gas pressure from molecular motion and calculate speed and transport scales using a locally specified Maxwell distribution.
Apply Stefan-Boltzmann, Wien and specified Planck laws to thermal spectra and radiative energy balance; state classical-model limitations.
Calculate heat, work, entropy and free-energy changes; analyze reversible and irreversible processes and engine or refrigerator cycles.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Animals and Comparative Physiology
decks.description: Explain animal form and physiological regulation across taxa.

includes: Animal diversity, comparative anatomy, embryonic organization and integrated physiology.

practice: Analyze noninvasive or supplied physiological records and anatomical images to test a homeostatic or comparative adaptation explanation.

outcomes.description: Compare major animal body plans, tissues and organ systems; trace fertilization, germ layers and basic organ formation.
Use feedback and mass-balance diagrams to explain neural, endocrine, circulatory, respiratory, renal, digestive and reproductive regulation.
Analyze comparative anatomical and physiological measurements; calculate clearance, gas exchange and energy budgets using explicitly stated compartment models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genetics
decks.description: Infer inheritance mechanisms from crosses and molecular evidence.

includes: Mendelian and molecular genetics, recombination mapping, population variation and quantitative-trait introduction.

practice: Infer a genetic model from crosses, sequence changes and phenotype data, reporting competing explanations and sampling uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Predict segregation, pedigrees and linked crosses; estimate recombination maps and test alternative inheritance models.
Explain DNA replication, repair, transcription, translation and mutation using strand polarity, sequence and chromosome representations.
Calculate allele frequencies and Hardy-Weinberg expectations; separate environmental, additive and nonadditive contributions in bounded trait models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology
decks.description: Connect plant form and physiology to environments and life histories.

includes: Plant diversity, anatomy, life cycles, growth, transport, photosynthesis and physiological experiments.

practice: Compare plant responses to an approved light, nutrient or water treatment using tissue observations and physiological measurements.

outcomes.description: Identify major plant lineages and tissues; trace alternation of generations, reproduction and meristem-based development.
Explain water potential, mineral transport, photosynthesis, hormone responses and source-sink allocation with bounded quantitative balances.
Measure growth, transpiration or photosynthetic response with controls; infer physiological limitations and distinguish stress from measurement artifacts.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry
decks.description: Obtain defensible quantitative chemical measurements.

includes: Chemical sampling, calibration, gravimetric and volumetric analysis, chromatography and electroanalysis.

practice: Validate an analyte assay in a realistic matrix using independent calibration, recovery, separation and uncertainty evidence.

outcomes.description: Apply locally derived electrode-potential and current-concentration models to potentiometry and voltammetry; diagnose interference and matrix effects.
Design sampling and calibration with blanks, standards and recovery checks; calculate uncertainty, detection limits and gravimetric or titrimetric results.
Explain partition and plate models; select and operate approved chromatographic separations and quantify resolution and analyte concentration.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry
decks.description: Predict inorganic structure and reactivity using working models.

includes: Periodic chemistry, main-group and coordination compounds, bounded ligand-field models and crystalline solids.

practice: Identify an inorganic compound from composition, geometry, magnetic and color evidence, stating limitations of the bonding model.

outcomes.description: Represent coordination geometries and isomers; apply explicitly taught ligand-field splitting and electron-counting procedures to spin, color and reactivity.
Explain main-group trends, acid-base behavior and redox stability using oxidation states, bonding and periodic evidence.
Construct unit cells and ionic-solid models; calculate stoichiometry, coordination, packing and defect charge balance.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Chemistry
decks.description: Predict organic reactivity from molecular structure and mechanism.

includes: Organic structure, stereochemistry, mechanisms and major functional-group transformations.

practice: Solve stereochemically explicit reaction sequences and perform an approved synthesis with yield and purity assessment.

outcomes.description: Predict and justify carbonyl, enolate, oxidation-reduction and functional-group interconversion products under specified reagent and solvent conditions.
Use curved-arrow electron accounting and reaction-coordinate diagrams to compare substitution, elimination, addition and aromatic reaction mechanisms.
Translate line, Newman, wedge-dash and Fischer representations; assign stereochemistry and compare conformational energies.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics and Kinetics
decks.description: Derive chemical equilibria and dynamical reaction predictions.

includes: Chemical potentials, nonideal equilibria, phase behavior, electrochemistry and mechanistic kinetics.

practice: Infer a reaction mechanism and phase behavior from equilibrium and time-course data, testing approximations against independent conditions.

outcomes.description: Derive chemical-potential and activity relations; calculate reaction equilibria, colligative effects and binary phase diagrams.
Derive electrochemical free-energy and Nernst relations; calculate cell potentials, equilibrium constants and bounded transport-limited behavior.
Derive and solve coupled reaction-rate equations, steady-state and pre-equilibrium approximations and Arrhenius parameter estimates.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Algorithms and Complexity
decks.description: Design algorithms with rigorous probabilistic and approximation guarantees.

includes: Randomized algorithms, concentration bounds, approximation, online algorithms and complexity limitations.

practice: Implement a randomized or approximation algorithm and present a complete guarantee proof with assumptions and adversarial cases.

outcomes.description: Construct greedy, primal-dual and relaxation-based approximations using locally developed linear-program duality; prove approximation and competitive ratios.
Prove time, space, oracle and communication lower bounds in specified models; distinguish unconditional results from complexity assumptions.
Derive Markov, Chebyshev and Chernoff-style bounds and use them to analyze randomized hashing, sampling and streaming algorithms.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Distributed Systems
decks.description: Build and reason about services under concurrency and failure.

includes: Distributed execution models, consistency, consensus, replication, partitioning and failure-tolerant operation.

practice: Build a replicated service and test partitions, crashes and duplicate requests against an executable consistency specification.

outcomes.description: Formalize clocks, causal order, asynchronous failure and consistency; prove bounded impossibility or indistinguishability results.
Design partitioned storage and retry-safe services; use fault injection to assess durability, observability and operational tradeoffs.
Implement a leader-based replicated log with elections and recovery; justify safety invariants and conditional liveness.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Methods
decks.description: Specify software behavior and establish machine-checkable assurance.

includes: Operational semantics, type soundness, temporal logic, model checking and program verification.

practice: Verify a small program and concurrent protocol, supplying specifications, counterexample traces and an explicit trusted-computing-base account.

outcomes.description: Specify finite transition systems in temporal logic; implement reachability and fixed-point model checking and explain state-space abstraction.
Derive Hoare-style verification conditions and loop invariants; use a taught proof-assistant or SMT workflow and assess trusted assumptions.
Prove progress, preservation and compiler-pass simulation for a small typed language with explicit evaluation rules.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Parallel and Scientific Computing
decks.description: Implement and validate scalable numerical computation.

includes: Shared-memory, message-passing and accelerator programming, parallel cost models and numerical reproducibility.

practice: Parallelize a numerical kernel on available hardware or emulators and submit correctness, communication and scaling analyses.

outcomes.description: Implement threaded, message-passing and GPU kernels for reductions, matrix operations or stencils; prevent races and invalid dependencies.
Derive work, span, communication and memory costs; partition data and identify synchronization and bandwidth bottlenecks.
Measure strong and weak scaling; compare numerical error, reproducibility, energy and performance across decompositions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Security and Privacy
decks.description: Design and validate defenses against explicit threats.

includes: Threat modeling, access control, secure protocols, cryptographic use, privacy and authorized defensive testing.

practice: Threat-model an isolated application, reproduce approved defects and demonstrate tested mitigations without implementing production cryptographic primitives.

outcomes.description: Explain security goals and assumptions for encryption, hashes, signatures and key exchange; compose established library primitives with correct key and nonce handling.
Test and harden an authorized service, interpret logs and justify remediation, disclosure and privacy tradeoffs from evidence.
Model assets, attackers and trust boundaries; analyze memory, authentication, authorization and input-validation failures.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis
decks.description: Prove and apply analytic-function methods.

includes: Analytic functions, contour integration, residues, conformal maps and analytic expansions.

practice: Solve contour and boundary-mapping problems, proving validity of branch choices and limiting arcs.

outcomes.description: Test complex differentiability, derive Cauchy-Riemann conditions and prove basic consequences of Cauchy's theorem and formula.
Calculate contour integrals and residues; evaluate real integrals and bounded inverse transforms with explicit contour-decay justification.
Construct Taylor and Laurent expansions, classify singularities and use conformal maps on elementary planar domains.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Geometry
decks.description: Calculate intrinsic geometric quantities in local coordinates.

includes: Curves, surfaces, smooth manifolds, tensors, connections and curvature at introductory intrinsic depth.

practice: Derive and compare geodesics and curvature for a plane, sphere and another explicitly parameterized metric.

outcomes.description: Calculate Levi-Civita connections, geodesic equations and curvature tensors from a metric; interpret coordinate-invariant curvature.
Calculate arc length, curvature, surface metrics and first and second fundamental forms for parameterized curves and surfaces.
Construct charts, tangent and cotangent spaces; transform vector and tensor components consistently between coordinates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Algebra
decks.description: Use graduate structural algebra in proofs and explicit classifications.

includes: Modules, Galois theory, commutative algebra and finite-group representations.

practice: Complete a structural classification project combining explicit computations with module, field or representation-theoretic proofs.

outcomes.description: Use localization, prime ideals and Noetherian conditions to analyze rings and elementary affine algebraic sets.
Compute Galois groups and intermediate fields and prove consequences for solvability and finite fields.
Analyze modules, exact sequences and tensor products; prove structure results over principal ideal domains.
Construct finite-group representations and character tables; prove decomposition and orthogonality results over the complex numbers.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure and Functional Analysis
decks.description: Prove graduate integration and functional-analytic results.

includes: Measure construction, Lebesgue integration, Lp spaces, Hilbert spaces and bounded operators.

practice: Prove a convergence theorem and solve an operator or variational problem, identifying exactly where completeness and compactness enter.

outcomes.description: Analyze completeness, duality and weak convergence in Lp, Banach and Hilbert spaces; prove projection and representation results.
Construct measures and measurable functions; prove and apply convergence, product-integration and Radon-Nikodym results.
Use bounded-operator, compactness and spectral results to analyze integral operators and variational equations under explicit hypotheses.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability Models and Statistical Inference
decks.description: Construct, fit and validate probabilistic models.

includes: Continuous multivariate probability, likelihood, regression, experimental models and Monte Carlo inference.

practice: Fit competing models to a designed or observational dataset; derive estimators for a simple case and validate software-assisted inference.

outcomes.description: Calculate densities, expectations, covariance and transformed distributions; derive conditional and multivariate-normal calculations.
Derive likelihood and Bayesian estimators, confidence procedures and likelihood-ratio tests for specified parametric models.
Fit linear and generalized linear models using stated least-squares or iteratively reweighted procedures; diagnose confounding, interactions and residual failures.
Construct finite Markov chains and Monte Carlo or Metropolis estimators; use a provided implementation and assess convergence and sampling error.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Point-Set Topology
decks.description: Reason about spaces independently of coordinates and distance.

includes: Topological spaces, continuity, constructions, compactness, connectedness and separation.

practice: Analyze a portfolio of quotient and product spaces with proofs, diagrams and counterexamples.

outcomes.description: Prove compactness, connectedness and separation results; use preserved properties to distinguish spaces and test homeomorphism claims.
Construct topologies, subspaces, products and quotients; prove continuity using open sets and compare metric and nonmetric examples.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics and Relativity
decks.description: Analyze constrained and relativistic mechanical systems.

includes: Variational mechanics, Hamiltonian phase space, symmetries and special-relativistic kinematics.

practice: Derive a constrained system in two coordinate choices and solve a relativistic threshold problem using invariants.

outcomes.description: Construct Hamiltonians, Poisson brackets and canonical transformations; analyze phase-space conservation and Hamilton-Jacobi examples.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations from stationary action in generalized coordinates; analyze constraints, symmetries and small oscillations.
Derive Lorentz transformations and invariant four-vector relations; calculate relativistic collisions, proper time and electromagnetic force transformations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Circuits and Instrumentation
decks.description: Build and characterize measurement electronics.

includes: AC and transient networks, semiconductor device models, amplifiers, sensors and sampled acquisition.

practice: Construct a low-voltage sensor amplifier, measure its frequency response and validate an acquisition pipeline against known signals.

outcomes.description: Acquire calibrated signals with a programmed interface; calculate sampling and quantization effects, noise spectra and aliasing using stated procedures.
Use bounded diode, transistor and operational-amplifier models to design bias, gain, filtering and sensor-readout circuits.
Solve RC, RL and RLC transients and sinusoidal networks using differential equations, phasors and transfer functions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electromagnetic Fields
decks.description: Calculate fields and electromagnetic energy from sources and boundaries.

includes: Three-dimensional electrostatics, magnetostatics, Maxwell equations, electromagnetic energy and simple radiation.

practice: Solve a symmetric field problem and an interface-wave problem, validating boundaries, dimensions and energy flux.

outcomes.description: Derive induction and Maxwell wave equations; calculate plane-wave propagation, polarization and interface reflection in linear media.
Calculate field energy and Poynting flux; apply explicitly derived dipole far-field formulas and distinguish near and radiation zones.
Calculate electric and magnetic fields and potentials using Coulomb, Gauss, Biot-Savart and Ampere laws and simple boundary conditions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Waves and Optics
decks.description: Predict wave propagation and infer optical structure.

includes: Oscillations, one-dimensional wave equations, acoustics, ray optics, interference, diffraction and polarization.

practice: Align an approved optical setup or analyze supplied patterns; recover aperture or wavelength and quantify resolution limits.

outcomes.description: Trace rays through lenses and mirrors; calculate image formation, magnification, numerical aperture and elementary aberration effects.
Calculate interference, slit diffraction and polarization using complex amplitudes and Fourier integrals; infer wavelength or aperture from patterns.
Derive coupled oscillations and the one-dimensional wave equation with locally defined partial derivatives; calculate modes, dispersion and acoustic intensity.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Computational Genomics
decks.description: Infer biological structure and variation from sequence data.

includes: Sequence alignment, assembly, variant and expression inference, phylogenetics and reproducible genomic workflows.

practice: Construct a reproducible sequence-to-inference workflow and implement its alignment or tree-likelihood core, auditing provenance and uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Fit read-count and genotype-likelihood models for variants and expression; control multiple testing and diagnose mapping, batch and population biases.
Implement finite-state substitution likelihoods on trees and compare phylogenies using resampling; distinguish ancestry from recombination and model misspecification.
Implement dynamic-programming alignment and graph-based toy assembly; analyze scoring, repeats, read errors and computational costs.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology and Virology
decks.description: Investigate microbial and viral mechanisms with controlled methods.

includes: Microbial physiology, horizontal gene transfer, viruses, culture, identification and antimicrobial evidence.

practice: Characterize approved nonpathogenic cultures or supplied culture records, reconciling growth, identification and susceptibility evidence.

outcomes.description: Use aseptic culture, dilution counts, staining and biochemical identification; interpret antimicrobial susceptibility and justify containment choices.
Compare microbial metabolism, growth, community interactions and horizontal gene transfer across bacteria, archaea and microbial eukaryotes.
Explain viral genome strategies, entry, replication and transmission; interpret plaque and infectivity measurements.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Neuroscience
decks.description: Connect neural electrical mechanisms to circuit and behavioral evidence.

includes: Membrane electrophysiology, neuronal dynamics, neural circuits, sensory processing and behavioral inference.

practice: Analyze supplied electrophysiological and behavioral records and compare passive, conductance-based and circuit-level explanations.

outcomes.description: Explain synaptic transmission, plasticity, sensory coding, motor control and major brain-system organization using circuit representations.
Derive membrane equivalent circuits and ion-equilibrium potentials; calculate passive responses and analyze explicitly specified conductance-based spike equations.
Interpret voltage-clamp, spike-train, imaging and behavioral measurements; distinguish correlational coding claims from causal perturbation evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Quantitative Ecology and Conservation
decks.description: Infer ecological processes and evaluate conservation interventions.

includes: Population and community dynamics, spatial sampling, ecosystem models and conservation decisions.

practice: Fit a spatial population model to survey data and defend a conservation decision under imperfect detection and competing objectives.

outcomes.description: Compare conservation and restoration actions using extinction risk, ecosystem function, uncertainty, distributional consequences and stakeholder obligations.
Analyze structured populations, competition, predation and resource cycles using matrix and differential-equation models with stability calculations.
Fit detection-aware occupancy and abundance models; use taught raster, distance and patch-connectivity representations to analyze spatial ecological evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Biochemistry
decks.description: Explain molecular catalysis and metabolic organization.

includes: Biomolecular structure, enzyme kinetics, metabolic pathways and bounded biochemical free-energy models.

practice: Analyze enzyme-rate and metabolic-label data, reconciling molecular mechanism, stoichiometry and energetic feasibility.

outcomes.description: Relate protein, nucleic-acid, lipid and carbohydrate structures to binding, folding and molecular recognition using sequence and three-dimensional representations.
Derive Michaelis-Menten behavior from algebraic steady-state rate balance; calculate inhibition models and distinguish affinity, turnover and cooperativity.
Trace carbon, electrons and ATP through central metabolism; apply an explicitly taught chemical-potential formula to coupling and pathway regulation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental and Sustainable Chemistry
decks.description: Infer chemical fate and evaluate environmental actions.

includes: Environmental speciation, atmospheric and aquatic reactions, compartment fate models, monitoring and sustainable intervention.

practice: Construct and validate a contaminant fate model from monitoring records and defend a remediation or substitution decision.

outcomes.description: Calculate aqueous speciation, partitioning, redox and photochemical transformations in explicitly defined air-water-soil compartment models.
Design contaminant sampling and analytical quality control; distinguish source, transport, degradation and detection explanations for observed concentrations.
Compare remediation and substitution strategies using exposure models, taught dose-response endpoints, mass balance, life-cycle boundaries and environmental justice.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Polymers and Soft Materials
decks.description: Connect polymer synthesis and molecular architecture to bulk behavior.

includes: Polymerization mechanisms, molecular-weight distributions, chain statistics, phase behavior and rheological measurement.

practice: Characterize a polymer series from synthesis and instrument records and test a structure-property model against molecular-weight and thermal evidence.

outcomes.description: Interpret size-exclusion calibration, calorimetry and rheometry; compare processing, degradation and recycling choices with uncertainty and material-life-cycle evidence.
Derive step-growth and chain-growth conversion and molecular-weight relations; predict architecture and dispersity from reaction mechanisms.
Use taught random-chain, mixing and viscoelastic spring-dashpot models to calculate size, phase behavior and time-dependent response.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Structure Elucidation and Spectroscopy
decks.description: Infer molecular structures from complementary spectra.

includes: Working IR, UV-visible, NMR and mass-spectral models and combined molecular structure inference.

practice: Solve a blinded structure dossier, including 2D correlation maps, and defend both the preferred structure and remaining ambiguities.

outcomes.description: Apply explicitly taught oscillator, absorption, chemical-shift, first-order spin-splitting and fragmentation models; state their assumptions and limits.
Infer molecular formula, connectivity and stereochemical constraints from IR, UV-visible, one- and two-dimensional NMR and mass-spectral evidence.
Assess peak assignment ambiguity, impurities, exchange and instrument artifacts; choose an additional measurement that discriminates candidate structures.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning
decks.description: Implement and evaluate predictive learning systems.

includes: Supervised and unsupervised learning, optimization, validation, uncertainty and responsible deployment evaluation.

practice: Implement baseline learners and one neural model, then produce a reproducible evaluation with calibration, ablations and a deployment-risk decision.

outcomes.description: Design leakage-free validation, tuning and calibration; assess distribution shift, subgroup errors, privacy and deployment consequences.
Implement regularized linear and logistic models, trees and a small neural network with derived losses and backpropagation.
Implement principal-component analysis, clustering and Gaussian-mixture expectation-maximization; interpret latent representations and identifiability limits.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Robotics and Autonomous Systems
decks.description: Integrate estimation and control in autonomous physical systems.

includes: Robot kinematics, bounded rigid-body dynamics, feedback, state estimation, planning and safety validation.

practice: Implement a simulated mobile or planar-arm robot with estimation, feedback and planning, then test sensor faults and safety constraints.

outcomes.description: Derive linear and extended Kalman filtering for explicit pose and sensor states; implement localization and evaluate observability and covariance consistency.
Derive planar-link kinematics and locally taught torque-balance dynamics; implement inverse kinematics and PID or linear-quadratic feedback with stability checks.
Implement configuration-space collision checking and sampling-based motion planning; evaluate failure recovery and justify operational safety limits.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Global Geometry and Algebraic Topology
decks.description: Compute and interpret global geometric and topological invariants.

includes: Fundamental groups, homology, differential forms, bundles and global geometric obstructions.

practice: Analyze a surface or bundle through coordinate calculations, chain complexes and an invariant-based impossibility proof.

outcomes.description: Construct vector bundles and connections from transition data; relate curvature and characteristic-class examples to global obstructions.
Calculate exterior derivatives and de Rham cohomology in elementary examples; prove and apply generalized Stokes' theorem.
Compute fundamental groups, covering-space examples and simplicial homology using presentations and boundary matrices.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: PDEs and Dynamical Systems
decks.description: Analyze continuous models through existence, stability and computation.

includes: Classical and weak PDE methods, nonlinear dynamical systems and validated discretization.

practice: Prove an energy estimate and implement a boundary-value solver with manufactured-solution and mesh-refinement tests.

outcomes.description: Solve one- and multidimensional heat, wave and Laplace boundary problems using characteristics, separation, Fourier expansions and Green functions.
Implement finite-difference and elementary finite-element schemes; derive consistency and stability conditions and test mesh convergence.
Analyze nonlinear ODE bifurcations, invariant sets and Lyapunov stability; distinguish numerical chaos from evidence of deterministic sensitivity.
Define weak derivatives and Sobolev spaces; formulate elliptic weak problems and prove bounded existence and energy estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Probability and Inference
decks.description: Justify stochastic and statistical procedures at graduate depth.

includes: Measure-theoretic probability, limit theorems, martingales, Brownian motion and asymptotic inference.

practice: Prove a statistical limit result and compare finite-sample behavior with its asymptotic prediction using a provided simulation implementation.

outcomes.description: Prove consistency and asymptotic normality for regular estimators; assess bootstrap, Bayesian and decision-theoretic procedures and failure cases.
Construct conditional expectations and prove laws of large numbers and central-limit results under explicit assumptions.
Analyze martingales and Brownian motion; define the Ito integral, apply Ito's formula and solve elementary stochastic differential equations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astronomy and Astrophysics
decks.description: Infer astronomical properties from light and dynamics.

includes: Astronomical coordinates, telescope evidence, stellar structure, planetary systems, galaxies and introductory expansion.

practice: Analyze public photometric, spectral and orbital observations to estimate an astronomical system's properties and identify degeneracies.

outcomes.description: Infer planetary and galactic masses from orbital data; interpret rotation curves, redshift-distance relations and competing matter distributions.
Use sky coordinates, parallax, fluxes, magnitudes and calibrated spectra to infer distance, temperature and radial motion with stated limits.
Construct hydrostatic and energy-balance stellar models; interpret evolutionary tracks and bounded nuclear-energy and radiative-transfer models taught here.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Fluids and Plasmas
decks.description: Model flowing and ionized continuous media.

includes: Continuum conservation, viscosity, diffusion, fluid stability and introductory kinetic and magnetofluid plasma models.

practice: Derive a channel-flow solution and a plasma dispersion relation, checking boundary conditions, scales and approximation regimes.

outcomes.description: Derive mass, momentum and energy balance equations, constitutive assumptions and nondimensional transport parameters in three dimensions.
Solve bounded viscous-flow and diffusion problems; linearize fluid equations to calculate waves and elementary instabilities.
Calculate Debye screening, plasma oscillations and charged-particle drifts; derive basic magnetohydrodynamic waves and compare kinetic and fluid limits.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Use quantum states to predict measurement outcomes.

includes: Quantum evidence, state vectors, measurement, one-dimensional wave mechanics and hydrogenic structure.

practice: Solve a barrier transmission problem and reconstruct a finite-dimensional state from specified measurement probabilities.

outcomes.description: Use locally developed spherical separation and angular-state notation to calculate hydrogenic energies, orbital probabilities and simple transitions.
Connect interference, photoelectric and spectral evidence to state vectors, operators, Born probabilities, uncertainty and unitary evolution.
Solve one-dimensional wells, barriers and harmonic oscillators with wavefunction boundary conditions; calculate tunneling and expectation values.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Statistical Mechanics
decks.description: Derive thermal behavior from microscopic probability models.

includes: Microcanonical, canonical and grand-canonical ensembles, quantum gases, fluctuations and phase transitions.

practice: Calculate an exactly solvable partition function and compare its behavior with a mean-field approximation and provided Monte Carlo results.

outcomes.description: Derive ensemble distributions and calculate partition functions, chemical potentials, thermodynamic observables and fluctuations.
Analyze lattice-spin and Landau free-energy models; calculate mean-field transitions, correlations and limitations near criticality.
Derive Bose and Fermi occupation laws from stated indistinguishability rules; calculate ideal-gas limits and degeneracy effects.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary and Quantitative Genomics
decks.description: Infer evolutionary processes from genomic and trait variation.

includes: Population-genetic processes, coalescent inference, quantitative genetics and genomic selection evidence.

practice: Compare evolutionary histories and trait models using simulated and public genomic evidence, including confounding and model-recovery checks.

outcomes.description: Derive elementary coalescent likelihoods and implement genealogical simulation; distinguish demographic, selective and recombination explanations of sequence patterns.
Derive Wright-Fisher and diffusion approximations for drift, mutation and selection; compare fixation and demographic predictions.
Fit additive genetic and mixed models with a taught covariance-estimation procedure; evaluate heritability, association, relatedness and prediction portability.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology
decks.description: Explain immune protection and pathology through mechanisms and assays.

includes: Innate and adaptive immunity, antigen recognition, immune regulation and immunological evidence.

practice: Analyze a controlled immune-response dataset and propose experiments distinguishing altered cell abundance, activation and assay interference.

outcomes.description: Trace lymphocyte development, receptor rearrangement, activation, tolerance and memory; predict vaccine and hypersensitivity mechanisms.
Interpret immunoassays and flow-cytometry gates using locally taught binding, compensation and control procedures; discriminate immune dysfunction hypotheses.
Explain barriers, innate recognition, complement, inflammation and antigen presentation in tissue and infection contexts.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular and Cellular Methods
decks.description: Design and interpret molecular and cellular experiments.

includes: DNA manipulation, quantitative molecular assays, protein methods, fluorescence measurements and experimental validity.

practice: Execute an approved molecular workflow or audit raw workflow records, including controls, calibration, sequence verification and reproducible analysis.

outcomes.description: Design biological replication, controls, randomization and normalization; analyze batch effects and justify biosafety, provenance and reproducibility decisions.
Design primers and cloning strategies; perform or audit extraction, PCR, gel separation, sequencing and bounded genome-editing validation.
Use taught binding and separation models for chromatography, immunoblotting and fluorescence assays; calibrate signals and identify specificity failures.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Epidemiology and Public Health
decks.description: Evaluate population-health evidence and interventions.

includes: Disease-frequency measures, epidemiological designs, introductory causal diagrams and public-health decisions.

practice: Investigate an outbreak or screening proposal using de-identified records, bias analysis and a justified public-health recommendation.

outcomes.description: Compare cohort, case-control and randomized designs; construct elementary causal diagrams and identify selection, confounding and measurement biases.
Calculate incidence, prevalence, risk ratios and diagnostic predictive values; analyze outbreaks with a taught discrete susceptible-infectious-recovered model.
Evaluate screening, vaccination and exposure-reduction decisions using absolute benefits, harms, equity, consent and evidence quality.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Inorganic and Materials Chemistry
decks.description: Relate inorganic structure and preparation to measurable properties.

includes: Molecular symmetry, coordination reactivity, inorganic solids, preparation and diffraction-based characterization.

practice: Prepare or analyze an approved inorganic material and distinguish candidate structures using diffraction, composition and property measurements.

outcomes.description: Derive Bragg and structure-factor models for simple cells; combine powder diffraction, spectroscopy and thermal data to infer phases and defects.
Design bounded solid-state, solution and surface syntheses; relate phase diagrams, defects and composition to ceramic, magnetic and electronic properties.
Assign point groups using locally taught symmetry operations; use supplied character tables and orbital diagrams to predict spectra and coordination reaction pathways.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Synthesis
decks.description: Design and evaluate multistep organic syntheses.

includes: Retrosynthesis, stereoselective transformations, organometallic coupling and synthesis validation.

practice: Design two routes to a stereochemically specified target and execute or audit an approved multistep sequence with full characterization.

outcomes.description: Construct retrosynthetic disconnections, synthons and forward routes accounting for protecting groups, functional compatibility and convergent strategy.
Validate intermediates and products spectroscopically; compare route yield, purification burden, hazards, material efficiency and reproducibility.
Predict chemo-, regio- and stereoselectivity in enolate, pericyclic, asymmetric and organometallic coupling reactions using taught mechanistic models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry
decks.description: Calculate molecular electronic and spectroscopic properties.

includes: Molecular orbital theory, Born-Oppenheimer approximation, finite-basis Hartree-Fock and theoretical spectroscopy.

practice: Implement a small SCF calculation from supplied integrals and compare predicted molecular and spectral properties against reference evidence.

outcomes.description: Construct molecular Hamiltonians, Born-Oppenheimer surfaces and orbital combinations; apply symmetry and variational reasoning to bonding.
Implement a finite-basis closed-shell Hartree-Fock iteration using supplied molecular integrals; explain basis, exchange and convergence limitations.
Derive rotational, vibrational and electronic transition predictions and selection rules; relate calculated intensities and energies to spectra.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Learning Theory and Advanced Models
decks.description: Analyze modern learning methods theoretically and experimentally.

includes: Learning guarantees, deep optimization, sequence architectures and probabilistic generative models.

practice: Reproduce a bounded modern-learning experiment with a derived objective, implementation, ablations and an analysis of theoretical versus observed behavior.

outcomes.description: Derive and implement attention, convolutional and recurrent computation with automatic-differentiation rules; analyze optimization and representation behavior.
Prove finite-class and capacity-based generalization bounds using locally developed concentration and symmetrization arguments; identify distributional assumptions.
Derive variational and diffusion-model objectives; implement bounded models and evaluate likelihood proxies, calibration, memorization and societal consequences.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Vision
decks.description: Infer scene properties from sampled images.

includes: Image processing, geometric vision, visual recognition and uncertainty-aware reconstruction.

practice: Implement a calibrated two-view reconstruction and a visual classifier, comparing geometric residuals with task-level error.

outcomes.description: Implement discrete convolution, Fourier image filtering, gradients, multiscale features and image registration; analyze noise and aliasing.
Train and evaluate convolutional recognition or segmentation models; distinguish semantic errors, dataset bias and geometric reconstruction uncertainty.
Estimate camera calibration, epipolar geometry, stereo depth and motion using least squares and a locally derived random-consensus procedure.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Calculate realistic quantum processes using controlled approximations.

includes: Angular momentum, spin, approximation methods, scattering, identical particles and mixed states.

practice: Compare approximation methods for an atomic perturbation and compute a spin-scattering or entanglement measurement prediction.

outcomes.description: Derive angular-momentum algebra, couple spins and calculate atomic fine-structure and selection-rule examples.
Apply stationary and time-dependent perturbation theory, variational methods and WKB with explicit validity and error reasoning.
Construct tensor-product and symmetrized states, density matrices and partial traces; calculate entanglement and elementary open-system evolution.
Calculate three-dimensional scattering amplitudes and cross sections using Born and partial-wave methods.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental and Computational Inference
decks.description: Design experiments and infer hidden physical parameters reliably.

includes: Instrument response, spectral and time-domain measurement, inverse physical models and advanced experimental judgment.

practice: Design and execute an approved spectroscopy or response experiment, implementing the forward/inverse analysis and defending its complete uncertainty budget.

outcomes.description: Design calibration, blinding and control procedures; justify apparatus, safety and reporting decisions through error budgets and competing experimental objectives.
Measure transfer functions, noise and spectral response; implement discrete Fourier analysis, convolution and bounded deconvolution with resolution checks.
Construct likelihood-based forward models and regularized inverse estimates; implement fitting and uncertainty propagation and diagnose nonidentifiability and systematic error.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity and Cosmology
decks.description: Calculate relativistic spacetime behavior and confront cosmological evidence.

includes: Tensor gravitation, Einstein equations, black holes, gravitational waves and cosmological models.

practice: Derive a spacetime observable and fit a bounded cosmological model to supplied distance data, testing coordinate and parameter degeneracies.

outcomes.description: Derive Friedmann expansion and linear density-growth models; infer cosmological parameters from distance and background-radiation summaries with degeneracy analysis.
Construct stress-energy tensors and derive geodesic and Einstein equations from stated variational principles with consistent tensor conventions.
Analyze Schwarzschild motion, horizons and weak gravitational waves; calculate redshift, lensing and orbital corrections.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Cell Regulation
decks.description: Infer regulatory mechanisms from molecular perturbations.

includes: Chromatin, gene regulation, RNA processing, signaling, cytoskeletal dynamics and causal perturbation analysis.

practice: Design and interpret a perturbation-rescue series that distinguishes two explicit cellular regulatory models.

outcomes.description: Explain transcriptional, chromatin, RNA-processing and translational control using sequence, occupancy and expression evidence.
Use time courses, localization, rescue and epistasis experiments to distinguish direct regulation, pathway order and alternative causal mechanisms.
Construct mechanistic diagrams for receptor signaling, feedback, cytoskeletal organization, cell-cycle checkpoints and programmed cell death.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Catalysis and Reaction Design
decks.description: Discriminate reaction mechanisms and design catalytic improvements.

includes: Mechanistic physical-organic methods, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis and evidence-driven catalyst design.

practice: Fit and challenge two catalytic mechanisms against kinetic and spectroscopic evidence, then defend an experiment-driven redesign.

outcomes.description: Construct organometallic cycles and surface microkinetic models with adsorption, site balance and deactivation; identify controlling regimes.
Design discriminating catalyst experiments and compare activity, selectivity, durability, resource use and scale-dependent hazards without assuming mechanistic uniqueness.
Derive competing catalytic rate laws and interpret isotope effects, linear free-energy relationships, crossover and time-resolved evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Theory and Computational Chemistry
decks.description: Use graduate molecular theory with explicit computational validation.

includes: Electron correlation, density-functional theory, molecular sampling, free energies and reaction dynamics.

practice: Implement molecular sampling for a bounded potential and compare calculated free energies or rates with higher-level supplied electronic calculations and measurements.

outcomes.description: Derive configuration-interaction and perturbative correlation approximations and Kohn-Sham equations; compare controlled calculations for basis and functional error.
Derive transition-state and bounded nonadiabatic reaction models; compare potential surfaces, dynamical trajectories and experimental rate evidence.
Implement velocity-Verlet molecular dynamics and Metropolis molecular sampling; calculate correlation functions and free-energy differences with convergence checks.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Condensed-Matter Physics
decks.description: Explain material properties from microscopic and collective models.

includes: Crystal and reciprocal lattices, phonons, electron bands, transport, magnetism and superconductivity.

practice: Calculate a lattice band or phonon model and infer material parameters from complementary diffraction and thermodynamic measurements.

outcomes.description: Analyze magnetic ordering and introductory BCS mean-field equations; connect collective predictions to heat-capacity, transport and susceptibility evidence.
Construct reciprocal lattices, diffraction conditions and lattice dynamical matrices; calculate phonon spectra and thermal contributions.
Derive Bloch, nearly-free-electron and tight-binding models; calculate densities of states, semiconductor populations and bounded transport coefficients.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
decks.description: Infer subatomic mechanisms from reaction and detector evidence.

includes: Nuclear structure, decay and reactions, particle symmetries, scattering observables and detector response.

practice: Analyze supplied decay or collision events, reconstruct a signal and distinguish detector effects from physical structure.

outcomes.description: Model energy loss, tracking, calorimetry and counting efficiency; reconstruct invariant masses and cross sections with backgrounds and radiation-risk judgment.
Apply liquid-drop, shell and tunneling models to binding, radioactive decay, fission, fusion and nuclear reaction energetics.
Classify particles and interactions by charges and symmetries; calculate decay and scattering kinematics and interpret weak, electromagnetic and strong processes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory
decks.description: Calculate and interpret relativistic quantum field processes.

includes: Classical fields, canonical and path-integral quantization, perturbative amplitudes, gauge symmetry and renormalization.

practice: Derive a scattering prediction through a bounded loop correction and demonstrate regulator-independent observables at the stated order.

outcomes.description: Derive propagators and Feynman rules; calculate tree amplitudes and representative one-loop integrals with explicit regularization and contour prescriptions.
Derive scalar, spinor and gauge-field equations and Noether currents; construct mode expansions and canonical or Gaussian path-integral quantization.
Renormalize a bounded perturbative model, derive scale dependence and use symmetry and power counting to construct an effective field theory.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology
decks.description: Explain how regulatory mechanisms construct organismal form.

includes: Animal and plant patterning, lineage, morphogenesis, stem cells and developmental experimentation.

practice: Reconstruct a developmental mechanism from lineage and perturbation records and propose a temporally discriminating experiment.

outcomes.description: Infer developmental mechanisms from lineage tracing, transplantation, live imaging and genetic perturbation, accounting for mosaicism and temporal effects.
Relate cell fate, adhesion, migration, division and tissue mechanics to morphogenesis, stem-cell maintenance and regeneration.
Compare positional information, morphogen interpretation and gene-regulatory patterning in plant and animal development.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Systems and Quantitative Biology
decks.description: Build and challenge quantitative mechanistic models of cells.

includes: Cellular dynamical models, stochastic reactions, parameter inference, experimental design and single-cell analysis.

practice: Fit competing regulatory models to perturbation time courses and single-cell evidence, then propose measurements that resolve nonidentifiability.

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric and regulatory ODE models; implement time integration and Gillespie event sampling and analyze stability and noise.
Estimate parameters with likelihood optimization; calculate sensitivities, structural or practical identifiability and discriminating perturbation designs.
Implement normalized single-cell factor models and neighborhood analyses; evaluate batch correction, trajectory ambiguity and multimodal biological validation.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Many-Body Field Methods
decks.description: Investigate interacting matter using advanced field and finite-system methods.

includes: Many-body Green functions, linear response, collective effective fields and controlled finite-lattice calculations.

practice: Compare a controlled finite-lattice calculation with a Green-function or collective-field approximation and identify which evidence would discriminate their predictions.

outcomes.description: Construct collective order-parameter actions and analyze symmetry breaking, fluctuations and renormalization near a specified transition.
Derive time-ordered and thermal Green functions, diagrammatic expansions and Kubo response; connect spectral functions to measurable observables.
Construct finite spin or fermion Hamiltonian matrices and use a provided eigensolver; assess symmetry sectors, finite-size scaling and approximation error.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Disease Biology and Translation
decks.description: Evaluate mechanistic disease models and translational interventions.

includes: Cancer and disease mechanisms, pharmacological response, causal translation and biomedical evidence judgment.

practice: Prepare an evidence dossier for a hypothetical intervention, fit a bounded exposure-response model and defend a translational decision without clinical recommendations.

outcomes.description: Compare cancer, degenerative, infectious and inherited disease mechanisms using cellular, developmental and immune evidence and model-organism limitations.
Derive bounded compartment pharmacokinetic and receptor-response models from locally taught first-order balances; estimate exposure-response and toxicity tradeoffs.
Evaluate target validation, preclinical reproducibility and trial endpoints; justify go/no-go decisions considering causal evidence, consent, equity and competing risks.
